title: Protocol for the induction of hindlimb ischemia and isolation of muscle endothelial cells in mice
protocol: Anesthetize the mouse with 3% isoflurane in 100% oxygen.
Remove the mouse from the chamber when it shows no signs of movement upon pinching.
Place the anesthetized mouse on a 37°C heating pad in the prone position.
Insert the mouse’s muzzle into an anesthesia mask for maintenance with 1.5% isoflurane and 100% oxygen.
Apply hair removal cream to remove fur from the hindlimb area.
Treat the skin of the hindlimb with iodine followed by 70% ethanol.
Make a small incision (1 cm) in the thigh after removing the fur.
Use a retractor to pull back the wound for better access.
Move the peritoneum proximally with forceps and cotton-tipped applicators to expose the incision area in the hindlimb.
Examine the neurovascular bundle using angled forceps and dissect it from surrounding tissues.
Separate the femoral artery and vein carefully, ensuring no damage is done to the femoral nerve.
Apply sterile 1× PBS to the exposed area to prevent drying out.
Use angled forceps to separate the femoral artery from the femoral vein.
Continue applying sterile 1× PBS to prevent it from drying out.
Thread a strand of 7-0 suture under both proximal and distal parts of the femoral artery.
Ligate using both strands with two knots each in the proximal and distal locations.
Cut off excess suture after ligation is complete.
Transect the femoral artery between the distal and proximal knots using spring scissors.
Remove the retractor.
Close the incision with size 6-0 silk sutures.
Inject the mouse via intraperitoneal (IP) injection with Meloxicam at a dose of 5 mg/kg body weight.
Apply topical lidocaine ointment to the sutured area.
Place the mouse on a draped heated pad in a new cage with fresh bedding.
Monitor the mouse continuously until it is awake.
Perform post-procedural care daily, including monitoring for signs of complications such as appearance, behavior, physical condition, and body weight.
Euthanize mice developing signs such as weight loss greater than 20%, wound infection, respiratory distress, or intractable dehydration.
Administer another dose of meloxicam based on pain criteria set by the laboratory if necessary.
Administer 1 mL sterile 0.9% sodium chloride subcutaneously for indications of dehydration.
Monitor postoperative observation including eating, drinking, and movement at least 5 times per week until the end of the experiment.
Turn on the LASCA and open its software.

Set up the LASCA software in a section of the project editor using the following parameters: Working distance: 10.4 cm, Measurement area: 2.9 cm (width), 2.2 cm (height), Point density: high, Resolution: 0.02 mm, Image capture frame rate: 6 images/s for 1 min.
Anesthetize the mouse with 3% isoflurane in 100% oxygen in the induction chamber to ensure the mouse is well anesthetized before positioning on the board.
Observe the mouse for any signs of movement.
Confirm the depth of anesthesia by pinching the mouse's paw.
Remove the mouse from the chamber and place it in the prone position on the LASCA plate with a 37°C temperature heating pad.
Administer a continuous flow of isoflurane to the mouse by connecting its muzzle to an anesthesia mask with 1.5% isoflurane and 100% oxygen.
Open a new file and position the visible red lasers (650 nm) at a region encompassing the hind foot to the toe of the mouse.
Press the record button to start acquiring the blood perfusion image.
Select the region of interest (ROI) in each ischemic region and uninjured region (internal control).
Calculate a mean value of perfusion for the selected ROI.
Repeat these measurements every week or as needed until the experiment ends.
Euthanize the mouse using CO2 for 5 min.
Spray the mouse with 70% ethanol to wet down the fur and treat the area around the hindlimb aseptically.
Use scissors and forceps to remove the skin from the whole femur.
Separate the medial thigh muscles from the femur bones where the distal and proximal suture knots exist.
Place the isolated muscle in cold 1× PBS.
Transfer the muscle to a microscope slide in a petri dish on ice.
Mince the muscle with a razor blade for 2–3 minutes until a fine paste results.
Transfer the minced muscle to a 50 mL tube containing 5 mL tissue dissociation buffer per mouse.
Vortex the tube for 3–5 seconds at the highest speed.
Incubate the tube in a shaking incubator at 37°C and 100 rpm for 45 minutes.
Optional: Vortex the tube for 3–5 seconds every 15 minutes during incubation.
Pass the single cell suspension solution through a 3 mL syringe attached to a 16 gauge needle 7–8 times.
Pass the solution through an 18 gauge needle until large particles are no longer observed visually.
Add an equal volume of ice-cold 20% FBS/1× PBS without collagenase IV to the tube.
Centrifuge at 4°C, 400 × g for 5 minutes and aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 10 mL ice-cold 20% FBS/1× PBS without collagenase IV.
Transfer the solution sequentially into 100 μm cell strainers, then 70 μm cell strainers, and finally 40 μm cell strainers.
Centrifuge the filtered solution at 4°C, 400 × g for 5 minutes and aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 10 mL ice-cold 1× PBS.
Centrifuge at 4°C, 400 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellets with 2 mL RBC lysis buffer.
Incubate at room temperature between 20°C and 25°C for 1 min.
Add 18 mL ice-cold 20% FBS/1× PBS to the tube.
Centrifuge at 4°C, 400 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 10 mL ice-cold 4% FBS/1× PBS.
Centrifuge at 4°C, 400 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 1 mL ice-cold 4% FBS/1× PBS.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube or tubes appropriate for endothelial cell sorting.
Prepare compensation groups as follows: Unstained group.
Mix Phycoerythrin (PE)-conjugated anti-mouse CD31 at a 1:300 dilution in 4% FBS/1× PBS.
Mix Fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)-conjugated anti-mouse CD45 at a 1:300 dilution in 4% FBS/1× PBS.
Add 1 × 10^6 cells in 250 μL 4% FBS/1× PBS to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add PE-CD31 and FITC-CD45 antibodies into the tubes, respectively.
Incubate the tubes at 4°C for 20 min in the dark.
Add 1 mL ice-cold 4% FBS/1× PBS to each tube.
Centrifuge at 4°C, 400 × g for 5 min using a microcentrifuge (model: Legend Micro 21R).
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 1 mL ice-cold 4% FBS/1× PBS.
Repeat step of adding ice-cold 4% FBS/1× PBS, centrifuging at 4°C, 400 × g for 5 min, and aspirating the supernatant twice.
Add 300 μL 4% FBS/1× PBS to each group tube (unstained, PE-CD31, FITC-CD45).
Transfer the mixture to a 5 mL cell culture tube and keep on ice in the dark.
Prepare several 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes containing 1 × 10^6 cells in 250 μL 4% FBS/1× PBS buffer per tube.
Add PE-conjugated anti-mouse CD31 antibody (1:300) to each tube.
Add FITC-conjugated anti-mouse CD45 antibody (1:300) to each tube.
Incubate the tubes at 4°C for 20 min in the dark.
Add 1 mL ice-cold 4% FBS/1× PBS to each tube and combine all tubes into a large appropriate tube(s).
Centrifuge the combined tube(s) at 4°C, 400 × g for 5 min and aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 4 mL ice-cold 4% FBS/1× PBS per tube.
Repeat steps involving resuspending and centrifuging twice more.
Resuspend the final pellet with ice-cold 4% FBS/1× PBS (250 μL/1 × 10^6 cells) and transfer it to a 5 mL cell culture tube.
Keep the prepared sample on ice in the dark until use.
Begin cell sorting within 1 hour.
Use PBS without Ca2+ and Mg2+ for step 47.
Add PE-conjugated anti-mouse CD31 antibody to a tube containing single cell suspension.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 20 minutes in the dark.
Add FITC-conjugated anti-mouse CD45 antibody to another tube with single cell suspension.
Incubate this mixture at 4°C for 20 minutes in the dark.
Plot cells for CD31 (PE) and CD45 (FITC) against an unstained control.
Sort endothelial cells from red polygonal gates on plotted data.
Record an unstained group as a negative control for each fluorescent intensity.
Run PE-conjugated anti-mouse CD31 group for the positive PE gate.
Run FITC-conjugated anti-mouse CD45 group for the positive FITC gate.
Adjust compensation settings with built-in program.
Prepare a 15 mL tube containing 7-8 mL of 20% FBS/1× PBS for endothelial cell collection.
Set both tubes on the cell sorter and run the sample to sort the targeted cell population (CD31+CD45-).
Sort at a rate of 1,000–2,000 cells/s with an efficiency >80%.
Use a nozzle size of 100 μm under 25 psi pressure.
Centrifuge the collection tube at 4°C, 400 × g for 5 min and aspirate the supernatant.
Store the pellet at −80°C for use in subsequent experiments or resuspend it with appropriate solutions for planned experiments.
Invert the collection tube containing 7–8 mL of 20% FBS/1× PBS several times before sorting to improve cell recovery.
